channel: Wikimedia Commons broad sweep (Category:AI-generated videos full recursive crawl + ~75 namespace-6 full-text searches + ~46 namespace-14 category searches) and Wikipedia-embedded videos (wikitext of 35 articles). Metadata via Commons API from the Higgsfield sandbox; primary-source date checks via developer pages / Wayback / arXiv / GitHub. No video frames were viewed by me: descriptions come from page text, prompts, ffprobe/API numbers, ffmpeg scene-change and luma statistics only (see notes on each candidate; Higgsfield video_analysis jobs were queued but had not completed when this file was written).

method_summary.commons_crawl: Category:AI-generated videos crawled recursively: 26 categories, maximum depth reached = 3 (there is no depth-4 level), 149 file pages (video + several still images). Second crawl of 13 related roots (AI-generated media, Text-to-video generation/models, Deepfake, MyHeritage/Grok retouched pictures, Wikimedia videos about AI, etc.) reached ~100 categories; only a handful of extra video files surfaced and all were political, brand, tutorial or audio items.
method_summary.commons_search: Full-text searches in namespace 6 with filetype:video for model names (Sora, Sora 2, Runway Gen-1/2/3, Stable Video Diffusion, AnimateDiff, Deforum, Pika, Kling, Luma/Dream Machine, Hailuo/MiniMax, Veo 2/3/3.1, VideoPoet, CogVideoX, Wan, HunyuanVideo, LTXV, Seedance, Grok Imagine, Midjourney, Make-A-Video, Imagen Video, Zeroscope, ModelScope, Kaiber, Wombo) and generic terms (AI-generated, txt2video, image-to-video, generative video, StyleGAN, DeepDream, VQGAN, Disco Diffusion, deepfake, Deep Nostalgia, first order motion model, Wav2Lip, neural style transfer, latent space interpolation) plus the Commons AI-template disclaimer phrase. Result: the category crawl is essentially exhaustive; searches surfaced no additional usable generative-video family.
method_summary.wikipedia: Wikitext (action=raw) of 35 articles read. Embedded videos found only in: Text-to-video model, Sora (text-to-video model), Veo (text-to-video model), Dream Machine (text-to-video model), VideoPoet, MiniMax Group, Will Smith eating spaghetti test, Deepfake, AI art (non-AI), Diffusion model (non-AI gifs). No embedded videos in Runway (company), Kling AI, Seedance, Generative AI, Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Midjourney, AI slop, Grok (chatbot), Google Flow, Genie (world model). Stable Video Diffusion, Deep Nostalgia, Video generation, Make-A-Video, Pika, Wan, LTX-Video, CogVideoX have no en.wikipedia article under the titles tried (HTTP 404).
method_summary.licence_stance: Commons tag PD-algorithm ('public domain because it is the work of a computer algorithm or AI and does not contain sufficient human authorship') is used as a stated basis. Where the uploader is also the generator and adds an explicit CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA dedication the verdict is 'clear'. Vendor-official demo clips that rely on PD-algorithm alone are 'likely' at best and are flagged as the weakest tier. Human-edited compilations, social-media rips, brand ads, political clips, clips of real people and clips whose generating tool is unnamed are rejected.

blockers: Video frames could not be viewed; all visual claims are inferred from page text/prompts and ffmpeg statistics. Higgsfield video_analysis jobs were still 'queued' at the last poll.
Commons has no files for Kling, Pika, Wan, HunyuanVideo, Midjourney video, Runway Gen-4, Luma Ray, Sora 2 raw outputs or Veo 3 Fast - those families cannot be sourced from Commons.
The original YouTube page for EXECUTE could not be retrieved (HTTP 429 / Wayback redirect loop), so its CC BY label rests on the Commons import template only.
PD-algorithm is a Commons community tag; for vendor-official clips (Sora, VideoPoet, Veo 3 Owl and Badger) no primary reuse licence exists - these are 'likely' at best.
Wikimedia upload servers rate-limited (HTTP 429) a first bulk probe; all 44 shortlisted media URLs were later re-checked with polite HEAD requests and returned HTTP 200.
